# vphyslite Total Solver — C89 / fixed-point / arena-only

A deterministic rigid-body and constraint core with an optional **Total Solver** orchestration layer.

The original physics capabilities remain available:

- rigid dynamic and kinematic bodies;
- externally supplied contacts;
- stable manifolds and warm starting;
- split impulse;
- sleeping islands;
- water and buoyancy;
- distance, rope, ball, spring, hinge, slider, weld and upright joints;
- motors, limits, breakable joints and physgun;
- events, debug draw, snapshots and host-driven CCD.

The new layer lets the same world consume two independent providers:

1. a **collision provider**, which appends contacts and optionally supplies sweep/TOI queries;
2. a **transform/math provider**, which reads and writes scene transforms and may replace any supported transformation operation.

Every math operation has an internal fixed-point fallback. A host can therefore supply all operations, only one operation, or none.

## Strict core contract

The files under `include/`, `src/`, `examples/` and `tests/` are:

- ISO C89;
- integer and fixed-point only;
- no `malloc`, `realloc`, `free` or hidden heap;
- no `float` or `double` in the strict core;
- initialized from caller-owned arenas;
- buildable with `-pedantic-errors`.

`compat/vp_fixed_float_compat.h` is an isolated migration shim for old host code. It is never included by the strict core.

## Total Solver pipeline

```text
external scene / animation / DSL
              │
              ▼
      transform provider
              │
              ▼
 pre-physics transform constraints
              │
              ▼
   kinematic/body pose transfer
              │
              ▼
       collision provider
              │ contacts / sweep TOI
              ▼
 existing vphyslite rigid-body solver
              │
              ▼
 post-physics transform constraints
              │
              ▼
      transform provider writes
```

The old `vpCallbacks` pipeline is preserved. When Total Solver attaches, existing callbacks are captured and chained rather than discarded.

## Transform authority

Each transform node chooses who owns the final pose:

| Authority | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `VP_TRANSFORM_AUTH_MANUAL` | Caller-managed node; may drive a kinematic body. |
| `VP_TRANSFORM_AUTH_EXTERNAL` | Scene/animation pose drives the body. |
| `VP_TRANSFORM_AUTH_PHYSICS` | Rigid-body pose is written back to the scene. |
| `VP_TRANSFORM_AUTH_BLEND` | External and physical poses are blended by fixed-point weight. |

Available transform constraints:

- parent;
- copy position;
- copy rotation;
- copy scale;
- look-at;
- distance;
- position limit;
- follow/socket offset.

Constraints have a pre-physics or post-physics phase, fixed priority and fixed-point influence weight.

## Collision provider contract

The collision provider does not need to own shapes or broadphase state. It receives the `vpWorld` and appends contacts using the existing APIs:

```c
static void generate_contacts(
    void* user,
    vpTotalSolver* total,
    vpWorld* world,
    vp_fx dt)
{
    VP_UNUSED(user);
    VP_UNUSED(total);
    VP_UNUSED(dt);

    vpContactsAddEx(world, bodyA, bodyB,
        point, normal, penetration,
        friction, restitution,
        VP_CONTACT_FLAG_NONE);
}
```

The contact normal points from `bodyA` toward `bodyB`. For a ground plane against a dynamic body, use world body `0` as `bodyA` and an upward normal.

The provider appends rather than silently clearing the raw contact list. This preserves:

- contacts added directly before the step;
- contacts generated by legacy `preStep` callbacks;
- contacts generated by the Total Solver collision provider.

## Provider-backed math service

The host may supply any combination of:

- compose;
- inverse;
- transform point;
- rotate vector;
- quaternion multiply;
- quaternion normalize;
- blend;
- look-at.

The same operations are also exposed as a service:

```c
vpTotalSolverMathCompose(total, &worldPose, &parentPose, &localPose);
vpTotalSolverMathTransformPoint(total, &worldPoint, &worldPose, &localPoint);
```

If the corresponding provider function is missing, the internal fixed-point implementation is used.

## Minimal setup

```c
vpWorldDesc wd;
vpTotalSolverDesc td;
vpWorld* world;
vpTotalSolver* total;

wd.maxBodies = 256;
wd.maxContacts = 1024;
wd.maxJoints = 256;
wd.solverIters = 12;

world = vpWorldInit(worldArena, worldArenaBytes, &wd);

td.maxTransformNodes = 512;
td.maxTransformConstraints = 512;
td.transformIterations = 2;

total = vpTotalSolverInit(totalArena, totalArenaBytes, world, &td);
vpTotalSolverSetTransformProvider(total, &transformProvider);
vpTotalSolverSetMathProvider(total, &mathProvider);
vpTotalSolverSetCollisionProvider(total, &collisionProvider);

vpTotalSolverStep(total, dt);
```

`vpTotalSolverStep()` attaches automatically on first use. `vpTotalSolverDetach()` restores the captured legacy callback set.

Set legacy callbacks before attaching. After attachment, replace them through `vpTotalSolverSetLegacyCallbacks()` rather than calling `vpWorldSetCallbacks()` directly.

## Build

```bash
make strict
make examples
make test
```

Or directly:

```bash
gcc -std=c89 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic-errors \
  -Iinclude examples/total_solver_demo.c src/*.c \
  -o total_solver_demo
```

The tests cover:

- strict C89 compilation;
- unaligned caller memory and aligned internal arena segments;
- legacy callback chaining;
- external math-provider dispatch and fallback;
- automatic collision-provider contacts;
- physics-to-scene writeback;
- socket/follow constraints;
- CCD fallback substepping;
- pair-cache replacement after more historical pairs than cache slots.
